source.citation: Written for Blackout, 2026-10-09, from the ABFM 2025 In-Training Examination critiques, items 4, 5, 15, 20, 21 and 25. Each question cites its item. Provisional grouping; review before trusting.

questions.q: Septic shock from pneumonia. MAP is 58 mm Hg after 30 mL/kg of crystalloid and antibiotics. What is next?
questions.why: Vasopressin is added only when norepinephrine alone leaves the pressure inadequate. Norepinephrine runs through a peripheral line until central access is in; it is never delayed for the line.

questions.q: How much crystalloid does the sepsis bundle call for in the first three hours of septic shock?
questions.why: With antibiotics inside the first hour. Boluses beyond that are judged by the response to each 500 mL, and many favour balanced crystalloid over saline.

questions.q: Thyroid storm after methimazole was stopped. Which drug is given first?
questions.why: Propylthiouracil drops T3 faster than methimazole, though the two have the same clinical outcome. Plasmapheresis is kept for patients who fail drug treatment.

questions.q: In thyroid storm, when is iodine given relative to the thionamide?
questions.why: Iodine blocks the synthesis of new hormone, but given before the thionamide it is substrate for the gland. The order matters: thionamide first, then the block.

questions.q: What does a glucocorticoid add in the treatment of thyroid storm?
questions.a: It blocks conversion of T4 to T3
d: It blocks synthesis of new hormone
It blocks release of stored hormone
It treats the adrenal crisis that always accompanies it
questions.why: Hydrocortisone or dexamethasone are the ones used, not prednisone. Blocking new synthesis is the iodine's job, once the thionamide is in.

questions.q: Epigastric pain on ibuprofen and nightly beer. BUN 37, haemoglobin 8.8, stable. What is next?
questions.why: The inhibitor starts on presentation regardless of when endoscopy happens. Endoscopy is urgent only with instability, lavage has no evidence behind it, and 8.8 is above any transfusion threshold.

questions.q: Upper GI bleed in a patient with coronary disease. Below what haemoglobin is transfusion recommended?
questions.why: Seven for most patients. The higher threshold also applies after recent cardiac surgery and in haematological malignancy. Embolisation is reached only after endoscopy fails.

questions.q: Forty-five minutes of nosebleed on warfarin, blood pressure 170/100, no orthostasis. What is the first step?
questions.why: Fifteen to twenty minutes of pressure on the lower third. If an anterior source is then seen, a vasoconstrictor or cautery comes next, and packing only after those fail.

questions.q: When is reversal of anticoagulation considered in epistaxis?
d: At presentation in anyone on warfarin
questions.why: A stable patient keeps the anticoagulant through the local measures. A mechanical valve, as in the exam case, raises the cost of reversal further.

questions.q: A pad an hour for six hours, haemoglobin 8, stable, breast cancer treated six months ago. What is given?
questions.why: Hormonal options are avoided where possible after breast cancer. Intravenous oestrogen is reserved for the unstable patient because it raises clot risk.

questions.q: A levonorgestrel IUD is placed for heavy menstrual bleeding. How long until the bleeding improves?
questions.why: Which is why it has no place in the emergency department, however good it is for the long term.

questions.q: A gunshot victim with capacity and a signed blood refusal directive is dying of haemorrhage. What is done?
d: His family consents on his behalf
Packed cells are given instead of whole blood
questions.why: Refusal directives are legally binding and physicians have been held liable for overriding them. Swapping the product does not change the refusal.

questions.q: When may a Jehovah's Witness be transfused?
questions.a: Incapacitated, with no refusal directive and no surrogate
d: When a court cannot be reached in time
questions.why: Capacity or a directive settles it either way. The exception exists only where there is no evidence of the patient's own wishes.
